security_audit.summary: All ten static findings are false positives. The matches are ordinary incident-response prose, Markdown resource links, and clear English rather than reconnaissance, shell execution, or obfuscation. Two medium-risk safeguards are missing: incident-data redaction rules and mandatory human approval before direct production deployment.

remediation.issue: Incident prompts request logs, traces, observability links, and production-like data without explicit redaction requirements.
remediation.suggestion: Require removal of secrets, personal data, customer payloads, and sensitive internal links before sharing incident evidence with AI tools.

remediation.issue: The immediate rollout option permits direct production deployment without a mandatory human authorization gate.
remediation.suggestion: Require authorized human approval, a tested rollback plan, and documented abort criteria before any production change.

remediation.issue: The duplicated extended-thinking paragraph creates long-line obfuscation alerts and exposes internal drafting text.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the paragraph with concise user-facing guidance and split long prose into normal Markdown paragraphs.

content.user_title: Resolve Production Incidents with an AI Workflow
content.value_statement: Production incidents are difficult to diagnose across logs, code, dependencies, and systems. This skill structures investigation, repair, verification, rollout, and prevention across specialized AI agents.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes error signatures, stack traces, logs, traces, timelines, and user impact through structured prompts.
Builds evidence-based root cause hypotheses using code paths, dependency checks, configuration comparisons, and git bisect.
Routes work to language, database, performance, testing, and security specialists.
Defines unit, integration, regression, security, cross-environment, and performance verification.
Plans canary, blue-green, immediate, or feature-flag rollouts with rollback and monitoring criteria.
Creates prevention tasks for documentation, linting, type safety, observability, and postmortems.
limitations: Does not connect to Sentry, DataDog, repositories, or deployment systems without separate tools and permissions.
Referenced specialist agent names may not exist in every Claude, Codex, or Claude Code environment.
Commands, thresholds, and templates are examples that require adaptation to the target system.
Does not replace human approval for production changes or expert review of sensitive incidents.

use_cases.title: Triage a Production Failure
use_cases.description: Organize error evidence, customer impact, recent changes, and immediate mitigation steps during an active incident.

use_cases.title: Coordinate a Cross-System Fix
use_cases.description: Route database, application, performance, and testing work while preserving context between specialists.

use_cases.title: Strengthen Incident Prevention
use_cases.description: Turn a resolved incident into tests, monitoring, static checks, documentation, and follow-up tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Triage an Incident
prompt_templates.prompt: Triage this incident: {summary}. Use {available_logs} and {known_impact}. Identify the error signature, affected users, timeline, and three immediate next steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage for a single production symptom

prompt_templates.title: Investigate the Root Cause
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate the root cause of {incident}. Review {stack_trace}, {recent_changes}, and {dependency_context}. Produce evidence-backed hypotheses, reproduction steps, and a git bisect plan when appropriate.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate investigation with code and change history

prompt_templates.title: Design and Verify a Fix
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a minimal fix for {root_cause} in {language_or_stack}. Include unit, integration, regression, security, and performance checks. Define rollback criteria and required monitoring.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a Complete Response
prompt_templates.prompt: Coordinate a complete response for {incident} across {systems}. Assign specialist roles and specify context handoffs. Deliver a root cause, fix plan, verification matrix, rollout strategy, and prevention tasks.

output_examples.input: Checkout requests began timing out after release 2.4.1. Sentry shows database timeout errors.
output_examples.output: Triage identifies release correlation, scopes customer impact, and prioritizes database traces. Next steps include reproduction, bisect, query review, and rollback criteria.

output_examples.input: A login endpoint may allow SQL injection after a recent query refactor.
output_examples.output: The workflow routes security review first, requires parameterized queries and regression tests, then verifies authentication controls before staged rollout.

output_examples.input: A frontend fix passes unit tests but may increase page latency.
output_examples.output: Verification adds integration testing, browser checks, baseline comparisons, and p95 measurements. Deployment remains blocked when thresholds fail.

best_practices: Redact secrets and personal data before sharing logs, traces, links, or production samples.
Confirm the incident scope, permissions, rollback plan, and success metrics before implementation.
Validate fixes in controlled environments before a gradual production rollout.
anti_patterns: Do not deploy generated fixes directly to production without authorized human review.
Do not treat a plausible hypothesis as the root cause without reproduction or supporting evidence.
Do not skip regression, security, or performance checks for high-impact incidents.

faq.question: What inputs does this skill need?
faq.answer: Provide a sanitized incident summary, error details, available traces, recent changes, business impact, and environment constraints.

faq.question: Does this skill execute commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow prompts and examples. Tool execution depends on the host agent, permissions, and user approval.

faq.question: Which technology stacks are supported?
faq.answer: The playbook covers Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, Rust, databases, performance engineering, testing, and security work.

faq.question: Can it work without an observability platform?
faq.answer: Yes, but conclusions may be weaker. Provide reproducible symptoms, application logs, test failures, and recent code changes.

faq.question: Does it handle deployment planning?
faq.answer: It creates rollout, monitoring, rollback, and abort criteria. An authorized human should approve every production change.

faq.question: How should sensitive incident data be handled?
faq.answer: Redact credentials, personal data, customer payloads, and internal tokens. Share controlled references only when the selected AI environment permits them.
